characters.name: George Bidwell
characters.description: Narrator and principal protagonist; American who rises in Wall Street, becomes involved with stolen bonds and later is tried and imprisoned in England

characters.name: Ed Weed
characters.description: Friend and early business partner of the narrator; introduced narrator to theatre, fashion and speculative life

characters.name: Harry
characters.description: A scapegrace young man in the narrator's circle who fires his imagination for Wall Street and worldly pleasures

characters.name: Waterbury
characters.description: Sugar broker who first employed the narrator

characters.name: Mr. Ambler
characters.description: Chief clerk and early benefactor who helps the narrator obtain a brokerage position

characters.name: John Morrissey
characters.description: Famous gambler and proprietor of faro banks and supper rooms frequented by Wall Street men

characters.name: Mike Murray
characters.description: Proprietor of an uptown gambling place mentioned among the gambling haunts

characters.name: James Irving
characters.description: Chief of the New York Detective Force (corrupt); cultivates and recruits the narrator into negotiating stolen bonds

characters.name: Stanley
characters.description: Detective associated with Chief Irving who participates in schemes described by the narrator

characters.name: White
characters.description: Detective associated with Chief Irving who makes business propositions to the narrator

characters.name: Hod Ennis
characters.description: Member of a gang who stumble upon the Lord bonds robbery

characters.name: Charley Rose
characters.description: Burglar and member of the gang that stole Lord's bonds

characters.name: Bullard
characters.description: Member of the gang involved in the Lord bonds theft; later goes to Europe and figures in other robberies

characters.name: Lord
characters.description: Wealthy investor (owner of the seven-thirties) whose office is burgled in the famed Lord Bond robbery

characters.name: Max Shinburne
characters.description: Educated German burglar who becomes 'Count Shinburne' in Europe after negotiating stolen bonds

characters.name: Francoise Blanc
characters.description: Gambling impresario (Blanc) associated with Homburg, Monte Carlo and Wiesbaden casinos

characters.name: Amstel
characters.description: Antwerp chief of police who investigates the Countess Winzerode affair

characters.name: Countess Winzerode
characters.description: Adventuress and gambler who marries Van Tromp and later reforms; central figure in a Paris/Antwerp intrigue

characters.name: Van Tromp
characters.description: Wealthy Antwerp gentleman (descendant of Admiral Van Tromp) whose marriage to the Countess produces scandal

characters.name: Edwin James
characters.description: Famous English Queen's Counsel (Q.C.) who forges post-obits and later falls from legal eminence

characters.name: Brea
characters.description: Associate who conspires with Edwin James in a forged will scheme for a large inheritance

characters.name: Sarah
characters.description: Mrs. Brea; daughter named in the forged will (referred to as 'Brea's wife')

characters.name: Ezra
characters.description: Shrewd lawyer who marries into the family and discovers a counter will; key figure in the Brea episode

characters.name: Eagan (will contestant)
characters.description: A nephew/relative who contests a will (appears in the forged-will narrative)

characters.name: F. A. Warren
characters.description: Alias/persona (Frederic Albert Warren / F. A. Warren) used by the narrator to negotiate with European bankers (central to the Bank of England operations)

characters.name: Lionel Rothschild
characters.description: Member of the Rothschild banking family; appears as accepting/handling bills in Paris/London

characters.name: Green
characters.description: Tailor (Green & Son) who introduces the narrator to the Bank of England and helps create the 'F. A. Warren' impression

characters.name: Mike Hurley
characters.description: Professional burglar enlisted by Irving for bank robberies in the Tweed era

characters.name: Patsey Conroy
characters.description: Professional burglar named among Irving's men

characters.name: Detective George Elder
characters.description: Detective who uncovers clues (memoranda) that foil one of the conspiracies in New York

characters.name: John Curtin
characters.description: Captain John Curtin of the Pinkertons; American detective who pursues and ultimately assists in capturing the narrator in the Caribbean

characters.name: Robert A. Pinkerton
characters.description: Member of the Pinkerton private detective organization engaged by bank agents to investigate in America

characters.name: William A. Pinkerton
characters.description: Variant reference to a Pinkerton agent (appears in dispatches/accounts); Pinkerton agency detective involved in the inquiry

characters.name: John Dobbs
characters.description: Burglar associate used by Irving in an attempted interception (appears in capture narrative)

characters.name: Edwin Noyes
characters.description: Clerk/messenger engaged as 'Warren's' agent; arrested in London and whose detention triggers wider events

characters.name: Major J. P. Roy
characters.description: Military officer at Governor's Island who receives custody of an extradited prisoner during U.S. transfer

characters.name: United States Marshal Fiske
characters.description: U.S. Marshal engaged in extradition proceedings and transfer of the prisoner to England

characters.name: Deputy Robinson
characters.description: Deputy marshal involved in escorting a prisoner for extradition

characters.name: Deputy Crowley
characters.description: Deputy marshal involved in escorting the prisoner to the steamer

characters.name: Deputy Colfax
characters.description: Deputy marshal mentioned as escort during removal of prisoner

characters.name: Deputy Purvis
characters.description: Deputy marshal present on the police boat escorting prisoners

characters.name: Chief Deputy Marshal Kennedy
characters.description: Chief deputy marshal involved in transferring the prisoner to the Battery and embarkation

characters.name: Peter Williams
characters.description: Solicitor for the Bank of England in New York who accompanies extradition activities

characters.name: Sergt. Edward Hancock
characters.description: London detective who assists in transatlantic transfer and investigation

characters.name: Sergeant Hayden
characters.description: Bow Street detective involved in pursuit and identification work (appears in transfer/extradition account)

characters.name: William Green (escort)
characters.description: Detective or official mentioned among those escorting the narrator (Green appears as an escorting officer)

characters.name: Inspector Wallace
characters.description: Police inspector who joins in meeting the arriving prisoner at Plymouth

characters.name: Sergeant William Moss
characters.description: Detective who is present during embarkation / escort events

characters.name: Captain (the little major) / Chatham Governor (unnamed)
characters.description: Prison governor / officer at Chatham encountered by narrator on arrival (portrayed as 'a cocky little major')

characters.name: Judge Archibald
characters.description: Judge who sentences the narrator and his associates to penal servitude for life at their Old Bailey trial

characters.name: Lord Mayor Waterlow
characters.description: Lord Mayor (Waterlow) who presides at public preliminary proceedings mentioned in the trial narrative

characters.name: David Howell
characters.description: Solicitor retained by the narrator and companions for their London defense (criticized in narrative)

characters.name: Mac
characters.description: Associate and co-conspirator who helps execute the forged-bills operations; frequently called 'Mac' throughout the narrative

characters.name: Maloy
characters.description: Irish local who helps the narrator during flight in Ireland, providing a jaunting car and assistance

characters.name: Austin Bidwell
characters.description: Narrator and author; prisoner at Chatham who spent nearly twenty years in penal servitude and petitions for release

characters.name: Heep
characters.description: Prisoner in adjacent cell to narrator; skilled artisan and repeated asylum/prison inmate with a turbulent past

characters.name: Joseph Matthews
characters.description: Assistant warder mentioned as having been in service twenty years and discharged in 1886

characters.name: my rat
characters.description: A young pet rat given to the narrator, tamed and taught acrobatic tricks; frequent companion in prison

characters.name: mouse / mice
characters.description: Small tame rodents kept by the narrator as pets and trained to perform tricks

characters.name: flies / fly
characters.description: Insects the narrator observed and tamed in the cell; described with observed behaviours

characters.name: Ross
characters.description: Principal officer at Chatham who delivers the news of the narrator's release and escorts him out

characters.name: Frederick Barton
characters.description: Young prisoner sentenced ten years for forgery; subject of a fabricated inheritance petition that led to his release

characters.name: George Smith
characters.description: Former clerk to auctioneers, prisoner who presents the forged petition at the Home Office and is instrumental in Barton’s release

characters.name: Niblo Clark
characters.description: Prisoner who composes a long, idiosyncratic petition detailing grievances and ill-treatment

characters.name: Foster
characters.description: Prisoner from Chicago who joins narrator's bricklaying party; former protege of the Christian Aid Society

characters.name: Turtle
characters.description: Former partner and confederate of Foster in criminal and corrupt political schemes in Chicago

characters.name: Stoneman
characters.description: American convict who became an accomplished burglar/express robber and was eventually sentenced in England

characters.name: Riley
characters.description: Confederate of Stoneman who is arrested and whose case helps bring Stoneman to trial

characters.name: Mrs. Riley
characters.description: Wife of Riley who participates in events surrounding Stuart and the lost money

characters.name: Stuart
characters.description: Well-known New York criminal lawyer who appears in the Stoneman/Riley episode

characters.name: Sergeant McCarty
characters.description: Former sergeant in the British army who joined the Fenian cause; sentenced to penal servitude for life

characters.name: William O'Brien
characters.description: Young Fenian recruit who was imprisoned and befriended the narrator; later opened a tobacco store in Dublin

characters.name: Curtin (dynamiter)
characters.description: Named among the dynamiters known to the narrator

characters.name: Daily
characters.description: Named among the dynamiters known to the narrator

characters.name: Dr. Gallagher
characters.description: Named among the dynamiters known to the narrator; described as having broken down under pressure

characters.name: Eagan (dynamiter)
characters.description: Named among the dynamiters known to the narrator

characters.name: Rev. Mr. Whitely
characters.description: Secretary of the Christian Aid Society who organized sending discharged prisoners to sea

characters.name: Sir William Vernon Harcourt
characters.description: Home Secretary referred to in petitions and correspondence regarding prisoners' releases

characters.name: Henry Mathews
characters.description: Named as "Her Majesty's Principal Secretary of State for the Home Department" in a petition included in the narrative

characters.name: James Russell Lowell
characters.description: American public figure who the narrator's supporters contacted on his behalf

characters.name: Mr. Blaine
characters.description: Secretary of State (U.S.) whose intervention on the narrator's behalf is mentioned

characters.name: Minister Lincoln
characters.description: U.S. Minister in London referenced as conveying representations to the English Government

characters.name: Lady Henry Somerset
characters.description: Supporter who took an interest in the narrator's case and helped press for his release

characters.name: Mrs. Helen Densmore
characters.description: Supporter living in London who aided efforts to secure narrator's release

characters.name: the Duke of Norfolk
characters.description: Prominent noble mentioned among those whose representations helped secure the narrator's release

characters.name: George Bidwell (relative)
characters.description: Relative/comrade of the narrator who was bedridden, campaigned persistently for the narrator's release

characters.name: Doctor Harrison
characters.description: Named in a petition as a medical authority who could confirm the petitioner's statements
